description:
Latitudes where a fixed star and a planet are angular at the same moment, which is how Brady tabulates a paran: not a place, a latitude. Twelve event pairs per star and planet (rise, set, culminate, anticulminate, minus meridian against meridian, which is a shared right ascension rather than a paran). Each row carries the houses of the technique in plain form: which body does what, the latitude, and the meridian where it happens at this chart moment. Solved on hour angles rather than by intersecting map polylines, so the latitude is exact rather than quantised to the polyline step.

[Group: Astro-Geography]
[Endpoint: POST /v1/parans/star]
[Cost: 50 credits (Tier 3)]

allOf.description: Birth data for a single natal chart. Required: date (YYYY-MM-DD), time (HH:mm:ss), latitude and longitude in decimal degrees. The short forms lat, lon, lng and tz are rejected with 400 INVALID_FIELD; pass the full names. timezoneOffset is hours from UTC and defaults to 0, meaning UTC; send timezone instead (an IANA name such as Europe/Kyiv, or auto) and the offset for that date is worked out, summer time included. city is a display label only: nothing here geocodes it, so it never stands in for coordinates. houseSystem is a single house-system letter, P by default; a name such as "Placidus" is refused, and the case matters because I and i are two different Sunshine systems.

ayanamsa.description: Sidereal school by name. Lahiri when omitted. Equivalent to ayanamsaId; send either.

timezone.description: IANA zone name such as Europe/Kyiv, or auto to look the zone up from latitude and longitude. The server takes the offset that zone kept at this local date and time, summer time included, and uses it in place of timezoneOffset. A clock time that happened twice takes the first occurrence; one skipped when clocks went forward takes the offset from before the change. Abbreviations such as EST are refused. Before 1970 the tz database is not reliable for every place, so send timezoneOffset when the local clock is known.

timezoneOffset.description: Hours from UTC at the given moment, not minutes. Fractional zones are hours too: 5.5 for India, 5.75 for Nepal, -3.5 for Newfoundland. Defaults to 0, meaning UTC. Ignored when timezone is sent.

horizon.description: Which horizon counts as rising. `geometric` (default) is altitude 0, the semi-diurnal arc as written in Meeus. `apparent` puts it at -34 arcmin, where refraction lifts a body into view first. Worth about two degrees of paran latitude at mid-latitudes, and refraction also breaks the equator mirror that the geometric horizon has, so it is a choice rather than a detail.

latitudeLimit.description: Search range either side of the equator, degrees. Default 60, which is the range Brady tabulates.

planets.description: Planet ids: 0 Sun, 1 Moon, 2 Mercury, 3 Venus, 4 Mars, 5 Jupiter, 6 Saturn, 7 Uranus, 8 Neptune, 9 Pluto. Default: 0-9.

stars.description: Star names from our fixed-star catalogue (GET /reference/fixed-stars). Default: the 36-star astrological set.

body.description: Birth data for star-planet parans. Coordinates are not used: a paran is a latitude, and which latitudes exist depends on the moment, not on where the native was born.

name: astroway_geo_parans_star
title: Star-planet parans (Brady)
